sources.scope: Original section text, equations and Figure 10 adjacent explanation inspected. Translation-only deformation with identity linear parts, changing weights and a gradient contribution to the normal transformation. No paper figure or implementation copied.

original_analysis: Chosen input-space weights 1−x and x blend identity with translation (0,0,1), giving F=(x,y,z+x). The triangle face normal becomes (−1,0,1)/sqrt(2), while both per-bone normal blending and inverse-transpose of the blended identity block retain +Z. A dimensionally explicit 3×3 Jacobian recovers the target direction.
limits: Authored shading normals need not equal individual geometric face normals.
The finite triangle and differential normal coincide here because F is affine.
Per-bone inverse-transpose blending and inverse-transpose of the blended linear block are not generally equivalent.
Stored vertex weights alone do not specify a unique continuous weight field or gradient.
Constant weights are a sufficient simple case, not a necessary condition for every correct result.
